name: CrystalTextLLM
one_liner: Fine-tuned language model proposes 3D crystal CIF files where sampling retries when a CIF cannot be parsed, and validity, M3GNet and DFT stability are measured afterwards.

loop.proposes: A fine-tuned LLaMA-2 model generates crystallographic information files (space group, lattice lengths/angles, fractional coordinates).
loop.judged_by: Pymatgen structural validators, M3GNet interatomic potential relaxations, and VASP Density Functional Theory calculations measure validity and thermodynamic stability afterwards.
loop.steers: Sampling retries when a CIF cannot be parsed, and conditional infill prompts steer generation.

headline_result: Nearly 90% of sampled structures pass geometric and charge-neutrality checks, and a high fraction relax to metastable or stable states in DFT.
caveat: Text-tokenized coordinates have finite numerical precision prior to force-field or DFT structural relaxation.
beyond_harness_note: Crystallographic geometry checkers and quantum-mechanical DFT relaxations measure validity and stability of the generated crystals afterwards.
generative_model: Fine-tuned LLaMA-2 70B on CIF crystal strings
algorithmic_authority: Pymatgen validator, M3GNet potential, and VASP DFT solver

sources.title: Fine-Tuned Language Models Generate Stable Inorganic Materials as Text (ICLR 2024 / arXiv:2402.04379)

verification.notes: Checked against Gruver et al., ICLR 2024.
